note: Real Oldham opportunities, gathered on 16 Oct 2026 from each organisation's own page (see `source`). Re-check every phone number, email and time before real use, and leave a field blank rather than guess. category is one of voluntary, paid_work, social_work. area is one of Central, East, North, South, West or 'All Oldham'. The top-level key is 'services' so directory.py can load it unchanged.

services.name: Volunteer with a local group or charity
services.description: Action Together lists volunteering roles with community groups and charities across {borough}, from youth clubs to food projects and befriending.
services.who_it_is_for: Roles for different ages and interests; each listing gives its own minimum age.
services.how_to_access: Search the Oldham roles online and register to express interest, or call or email the volunteering team for a chat first.

services.name: Oldham Youth Council
services.description: Elected young people who campaign on the issues that matter to young people in {borough}. Youth Council Champions make films, design posters and run events.
services.how_to_access: Wednesdays 6pm to 8:30pm at Rock Street Resource Centre, Rock Street, OL1 3UJ. Contact the youth service before your first visit.

services.name: Duke of Edinburgh's Award
services.description: Volunteering, a skill, physical activity and an expedition, recognised by employers and colleges. Youth Council Champion work in {borough} can count towards it.
services.how_to_access: Ask your school, college or youth centre if they run it, or find a centre on the DofE website.

services.name: Mentor a young person leaving care
services.description: Guide a young person who is leaving care. No experience needed: training, ongoing support and supervision are given, and expenses are paid.
services.who_it_is_for: Adults who want to support a young person. Check the minimum age with the co-ordinator.
services.how_to_access: Call the Mentoring Project Co-ordinator to find out more.

services.name: Youth Hub with Get Oldham Working
services.provider: {borough} Council, Positive Steps and Jobcentre Plus
services.description: One place in the town centre for help finding a job, an apprenticeship or training, or getting back into learning. Get Oldham Working, Positive Steps and a Youth Jobcentre Plus worker are all there.
services.how_to_access: Drop in on Union Street, Oldham town centre (22 Union Street, OL1 1BE), Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm, or call or email first.

services.name: Empower Oldham
services.description: Mentoring and practical help for young people not in education, work or training: CV and job search clinics, mock interviews, work experience, CSCS and first aid courses, maths and English, and social activities.
services.who_it_is_for: 16 to 19 year olds not in education, work or training; up to 25 if care experienced or with an EHCP. Places are limited.
services.how_to_access: Contact the team directly; young people and parents or carers can get in touch.

services.name: Careers guidance
services.description: Careers advisers, coaches and youth engagement workers help you work out what you want to do next and how to get there.
services.who_it_is_for: Young people after school, and 19 to 25 year olds with an EHCP.
services.how_to_access: Call or email, or visit Medtia Place, 80 Union Street, OL1 1DJ, Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm.

services.name: Apprenticeships at Oldham College
services.description: Earn while you learn. Oldham College and the council are working with local employers to create apprenticeships for young people, including Foundation Apprenticeships with extra support.
services.how_to_access: Look at the college's apprenticeship pages and contact the Apprenticeship Team.

services.name: Jobs Guarantee: six months of paid work
services.description: A paid six-month job, 25 hours a week, with wages funded by the government, to build experience and a reference.
services.who_it_is_for: 18 to 24 year olds who have been on Universal Credit and looking for work for 18 months or more.
services.how_to_access: Ask your Jobcentre Plus work coach whether you could be referred.

services.name: Find an apprenticeship
services.description: Search paid apprenticeships near {borough}, from engineering and construction to care and business.
services.who_it_is_for: 16 and over, not in full-time education.
services.how_to_access: Search by postcode district and set up alerts.

services.name: Free careers adviser
services.description: Free one-to-one careers advice from a qualified adviser: what to aim for, CVs, courses and changing direction. Since 1 October 2026 the National Careers Service's advisers are part of DWP.
services.who_it_is_for: Anyone 18 or over in England, including people who are already working. Under 18 and not in education or training can also use it.
services.how_to_access: Call 0800 072 0288, Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm, free from landlines and most mobiles.

services.name: Free youth clubs across Oldham
services.description: Free drop-in evening clubs with youth workers in Shaw, Chadderton, Failsworth, Sholver, Hathershaw, Alt and Limeside. A good way to meet people and build confidence.
services.how_to_access: Just turn up. Times and venues are on the youth service page, for example Shaw Youth Club on Tuesdays 6pm to 8pm.

services.name: Mahdlo Youth Zone
services.description: Sport, arts, music, climbing and cooking, open seven days a week. Membership is 5 pounds a year, then 50p a visit.
services.who_it_is_for: 8 to 19 year olds, or up to 25 with an additional need or disability.
services.how_to_access: Join online or at reception. Egerton Street, OL1 3SE, opposite Blue Coat School (buses 76, 403, 411, 893).

services.name: Barrier Breakers
services.description: A weekly group for young people with additional needs or disabilities, part of the Youth Voice Family with the Youth Council.
services.who_it_is_for: 11 to 21 year olds with additional needs or disabilities.
services.how_to_access: Mondays 6pm to 8pm at Rock Street Resource Centre, OL1 3UJ. Contact the team before you go.

services.name: Oldham Young Carers
services.description: Weekly groups, breaks and support for young people who help look after someone at home.
services.how_to_access: Fill in the young carers referral form on the Positive Steps website, or call for help with it.

services.name: Oldham Theatre Workshop
services.description: Acting, music, dance and design with other young people.
services.how_to_access: See the website for sessions and how to join.

services.name: Youth Guarantee: training, work experience or an apprenticeship
services.description: Support from a work coach to get ready for work and into a job: sector-based work academies, 2 to 8 weeks of work experience, CV and interview sessions, or an apprenticeship. Travel and childcare costs can be paid back, and Universal Credit carries on.
services.who_it_is_for: 16 to 24 year olds getting Universal Credit.
services.how_to_access: Ask your work coach at the jobcentre, at the start of your claim or later.

services.name: Help to earn more in the job you have
services.description: If you're working but on low pay, a work coach can help with CVs, skills training and moving up or into the field you want. Travel and childcare costs can be covered.
services.who_it_is_for: People in work on low earnings who get Universal Credit.
services.how_to_access: Send a message in your Universal Credit journal asking for in-work progression support.
